name: Louis Malle
milestone_by_age_26: Co-directed the documentary The Silent World with Jacques Cousteau (1956), which won the Palme d'Or at Cannes and the Academy Award for Best Documentary.
early_history_summary: Born into a wealthy industrialist family in northern France, Malle studied political science at Sciences Po before switching to film at IDHEC. At age 22 he joined Jacques Cousteau's expedition as co-director and cameraman, resulting in the landmark underwater documentary The Silent World (1956), which won the Palme d'Or at Cannes when Malle was just 23.
family_context_summary: Born into the wealthy Béghin-Malle industrialist family in Thumeries; his mother Françoise was from the Béghin sugar dynasty and his father Pierre was an industrialist. The family did not approve of his film career choice.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family involvement in film or the arts; the family wealth came from sugar and industrial enterprises.
primary_early_advantage_tags: wealthy family, IDHEC, Cousteau mentorship, French cinema, Paris, WWII experience
evidence_summary: Malle was born into the wealthy Béghin sugar industrialist family, providing financial safety and access to elite French institutions. He studied at Sciences Po and IDHEC, then was chosen by Jacques Cousteau to co-direct The Silent World (1956), winning the Palme d'Or at age 23. His WWII experience of witnessing a Gestapo raid on his boarding school shaped his later autobiographical film Au revoir les enfants. The French cinema renaissance of the 1950s provided a structural wave, and his mentorship under Cousteau and Bresson gave him elite ecosystem access at a remarkably young age.
starting_point: Born into a wealthy industrialist family in Thumeries, France; mother from the Béghin sugar dynasty, father an industrialist; raised Catholic despite part-Jewish heritage.
current_position: Died in November 1995 at age 63 in Beverly Hills; final films include Au revoir les enfants (1987) and Vanya on 42nd Street (1994); three-time Oscar nominee and two-time Golden Lion winner.

trajectory.event: Joined Jacques Cousteau's Calypso expedition as co-director and cameraman, beginning work on The Silent World.
The Silent World won the Palme d'Or at Cannes and later the Academy Award for Best Documentary.
Assisted Robert Bresson on A Man Escaped and directed his first feature film, Elevator to the Gallows, featuring a Miles Davis score.
The Lovers won the Special Jury Prize at Venice Film Festival and sparked international controversy for its sexual content.
Directed Lacombe, Lucien, a controversial film about wartime collaboration, nominated for the Best Foreign Language Film Oscar.
Au revoir les enfants, based on his childhood WWII experience, won the Golden Lion at Venice and was nominated for Best Foreign Language Film Oscar.
Made a Fellow of the British Academy of Film and Television Arts (BAFTA).
Died of cancer in Beverly Hills on November 23, 1995.

name: Sammy Sosa
milestone_by_age_26: Made MLB debut on June 16, 1989 with the Texas Rangers at age 20, becoming the youngest Dominican player to appear in the major leagues.
early_history_summary: Growing up in extreme poverty in the Dominican Republic after his father's death when he was seven, Sosa shined shoes and sold oranges before starting baseball at age 14. He signed with the Texas Rangers at age 16 for a $3,500 bonus and rose rapidly through the minor leagues to reach the majors by age 20.
family_context_summary: Born to a poor family in Consuelo, Dominican Republic; father died of a brain aneurysm when Sosa was seven, leaving his mother to raise seven children in poverty. Sosa worked from age six shining shoes and selling oranges to help support the family.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of parental involvement in baseball or sports; Sosa's father was a tractor driver at a sugarcane plantation and his mother was a housemaid.
primary_early_advantage_tags: extreme poverty, fatherless, Dominican baseball pipeline, raw talent, San Pedro de Macoris
evidence_summary: Sosa grew up in extreme poverty in the Dominican Republic, losing his father at age seven and working from childhood to support his family. He did not start playing organized baseball until age 14, but showed enough raw talent to be signed by the Texas Rangers at 16. San Pedro de Macorís, his hometown region, is one of the most productive baseball talent hotbeds in the world, providing a natural pipeline to the major leagues. His rapid ascent from poverty to MLB debut at 20 was driven by physical talent and the Dominican baseball ecosystem rather than family resources or formal training.
starting_point: Born into extreme poverty in Consuelo, Dominican Republic; father was a sugarcane plantation tractor driver who died when Sosa was seven; mother worked as a housemaid raising seven children.
current_position: Retired from MLB in 2007 after 18 seasons; resides in the Dominican Republic; estimated net worth approximately $60-70 million; 7-time All-Star and 1998 NL MVP with 609 career home runs.

trajectory.event: Signed with the Texas Rangers for a $3,500 bonus, giving most of the money to his mother.
Made MLB debut on June 16 with the Texas Rangers, becoming the youngest Dominican to play in the majors.
Traded to the Chicago Cubs, where he would spend the peak of his career.
Hit 66 home runs in the famous home run race with Mark McGwire, winning NL MVP and the Roberto Clemente Award.
Became the first player in MLB history to hit 60+ home runs in two consecutive seasons.
Played his final MLB season with the Texas Rangers, reaching 609 career home runs.

name: Leonid Popov
milestone_by_age_26: Selected as a Soviet cosmonaut on April 27, 1970 at age 24, joining Air Force Group 5 through the highly competitive Soviet space program selection process.
early_history_summary: Born in Oleksandriia, Ukrainian SSR, Popov graduated from the Higher Air Force School in Chernigov with a degree in electrical engineering in 1968. He was selected into the Soviet cosmonaut corps in 1970 and went on to command three space missions including Soyuz 35, logging over 200 days in space.
family_context_summary: Born in Oleksandriia, Kirovohrad Oblast, Ukrainian SSR; no documented information about family financial status or parental occupations in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet Air Force, cosmonaut selection, military aviation, electrical engineering, space program
evidence_summary: Popov's path to becoming a cosmonaut was driven by the Soviet military aviation pipeline: he graduated from the Higher Air Force School in Chernigov (1968) and was selected into the cosmonaut corps in 1970 at age 24. The Soviet space program was at its peak during this period, and selection into the cosmonaut corps was extremely competitive. No family background information was found in reviewed sources, suggesting his advancement came through the institutional pipeline rather than family connections.
starting_point: Born in Oleksandriia, Ukrainian SSR; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from active cosmonaut duty in 1987 and from military service in 1995 as a Major General in the Soviet Air Force; twice Hero of the Soviet Union; living in retirement.

trajectory.event: Graduated from the Higher Air Force School in Chernigov with a degree in electrical engineering.
Selected as a cosmonaut in Soviet Air Force Group 5 on April 27, 1970.
Commanded Soyuz 35 on a long-duration mission to Salyut 6, spending over 184 days in space; awarded Hero of the Soviet Union.
Commanded Soyuz 40 mission; awarded a second Hero of the Soviet Union.
Commanded Soyuz T-7 mission to Salyut 7.
Retired from active cosmonaut duty after logging 200 days, 14 hours, and 45 minutes in space across three missions.

name: Ricardo Rodríguez
milestone_by_age_26: Finished second at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1960 at age 18 (youngest ever Le Mans podium), then became the youngest Formula One driver to start from the front row at the 1961 Italian Grand Prix with Ferrari at age 19.
early_history_summary: Born to a wealthy Mexican family, Rodríguez began racing as a young teenager and won his first international sportscar race at Riverside in 1957 at age 15. He was refused entry to Le Mans in 1958 for being too young but returned to finish second in 1960, earning a Ferrari F1 drive at 19.
family_context_summary: Born to a very wealthy Mexican family in Mexico City; his father spent freely on the brothers' racing careers, buying them Corvettes and Porsches and supporting their transition from motorcycles to cars in their early teens.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a wealthy businessman and racing enthusiast who fully funded the Rodríguez brothers' motorsport careers from a young age, providing cars, equipment, and entry to international events.
primary_early_advantage_tags: wealthy father, Ferrari, Le Mans, brother Pedro, prodigy, early racing, sportscar racing
evidence_summary: Rodríguez was a genuine racing prodigy born to a wealthy Mexican family that fully funded his career from childhood. His father bought them sports cars and paid for international competition. By 15 he won his first international race; by 18 he finished second at Le Mans (youngest ever podium); by 19 he qualified second for his F1 debut with Ferrari at Monza. His older brother Pedro was also a top racing driver, creating a high-trust sibling partnership. Luigi Chinetti, the NART founder, served as mentor and advocate to Enzo Ferrari. Rodríguez died at age 20 in practice for the 1962 Mexican Grand Prix, cutting short one of motorsport's most promising careers.
starting_point: Born to a very wealthy Mexican family in Mexico City; father was a businessman and racing enthusiast who fully funded the racing careers of Ricardo and his older brother Pedro from their early teens.
current_position: Died on November 1, 1962 at age 20 in a crash during practice for the inaugural Mexican Grand Prix in Mexico City; was a Ferrari Formula One driver and Le Mans podium finisher.

trajectory.event: Won his first international sportscar race at Riverside, California, demonstrating prodigious talent at a young age.

Scored his first F1 championship points with fourth place at the Belgian Grand Prix; died on November 1 in practice for the Mexican Grand Prix.

name: Jet Li
milestone_by_age_26: Won the first of five consecutive Chinese national wushu all-around championships in 1974 at age 11, and toured the United States performing for President Nixon at the White House.
early_history_summary: Born in Beijing, Li's father died when he was two, leaving the family in poverty. At age eight he was selected from over 1,000 children for wushu training at the Beijing Shichahai Sports School. His coach Wu Bin made extraordinary efforts including buying food for Li's family. By age 11 he won the national all-around youth championship and by 12 was competing against adults.
family_context_summary: Born in Beijing as the youngest of five children; father died when Li was two years old, leaving the family in poverty. His mother raised the family alone in difficult circumstances.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family involvement in martial arts or sports; Li was discovered through a school summer program and developed through the state sports system.
primary_early_advantage_tags: wushu prodigy, Beijing sports school, coach Wu Bin, national champion, poverty, state sports system, Cultural Revolution
evidence_summary: Li was a genuine wushu prodigy selected from over 1,000 children at age eight by coaches at the Beijing Shichahai Sports School. His coach Wu Bin made extraordinary personal efforts, including buying food for Li's impoverished family to ensure adequate protein intake. Li won the national all-around championship at age 11 and continued for five consecutive years (1974-1979), competing against adults from age 12. The Chinese state sports system provided the institutional pipeline, while the post-Cultural Revolution revival of martial arts created a structural wave. Despite family poverty and the loss of his father at age two, Li's physical talent and intensive training from age eight produced extraordinary early achievement.
starting_point: Born in Beijing as the youngest of five children; father died when Li was two, leaving the family in poverty; raised by his mother alone in difficult financial circumstances.
current_position: Retired from acting due to hyperthyroidism and health issues; resides in Singapore (citizen since 2009); estimated net worth approximately $250 million; founder of The One Foundation philanthropy.

name: Alexander Vinokourov
milestone_by_age_26: Turned professional with the Casino-Ag2r cycling team in 1998 at age 24, after rising through the Soviet and Kazakhstani amateur cycling systems and completing a year with the French amateur team EC Saint-Étienne Loire.
early_history_summary: Born in Petropavl, Kazakh SSR, Vinokourov began cycling at age 11 in 1984 through the local Children and Youth Sports School. At 13 he entered a sports school in Almaty for five years of intensive training, followed by Soviet national team duty during military service. After Kazakhstan's independence, he moved to France in 1997 to race as an amateur before turning professional in 1998.
family_context_summary: Born to farming parents in Petropavl, Kazakh SSR; no evidence of family wealth or cycling background. His father Nikolay reported that Vinokourov began cycling at age 11 through the local Children and Youth Sports School.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; family were farmers with no known connection to cycling.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet sports school, cycling from age 11, Almaty training, national team, post-Soviet transition, intensive training
evidence_summary: Vinokourov's path to professional cycling was shaped by the Soviet sports system: he started cycling at 11, entered a specialized sports school in Almaty at 13, and trained as part of the Soviet national team during military service. The training was extraordinarily intense, with sessions up to three times daily. After Kazakhstan's independence, he transitioned to French amateur racing in 1997 before turning professional with Casino-Ag2r in 1998 at age 24. His family were farmers with no cycling background, and his advancement came through institutional selection and relentless training rather than family resources.
starting_point: Born to farming parents in Petropavl, Kazakh SSR, Soviet Union; family had no cycling background or notable financial resources.
current_position: General manager of UCI WorldTeam XDS Astana Team; former Olympic gold medalist (2012 road race) and Vuelta a España champion (2006); estimated net worth in the low millions; resides in Kazakhstan and Monaco.

trajectory.event: Began cycling at the Petropavl Children and Youth Sports School, training daily and competing in cyclo-cross.

Won the Vuelta a España overall classification, his first Grand Tour victory.
Caught blood doping during the Tour de France, receiving a two-year suspension from competition.
Won the Olympic gold medal in the men's road race in London, then retired from professional cycling.
